specs.anchorText: Everything in the rest of the chapter is this block applied to patches.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a friendly cartoon photograph cut into a tidy grid of square paper patches, and each little square patch is an expressive cartoon character holding a small megaphone and a paper contact-list, all cheerfully shouting to every other patch across the whole picture, colorful thin connection lines linking each patch to all the others like a chatty group conversation. Off to one side, a slightly grumpy little convolution character with a tiny fixed window peeks at only its three nearest neighbors, looking left out. The style is friendly and approachable, like an XKCD-inspired infographic meets Kurzgesagt, soft pastel blues, greens, and warm orange, expressive simple shapes, minimal visual clutter. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. Keep the composition simple and focused on the one clear metaphor: every patch talks to every other patch at once.
specs.alt: A photograph cut into a grid of square patches where each patch is a cartoon character holding a megaphone and a contact list, all shouting to every other patch across colorful connection lines, while a small convolution character with a tiny fixed window peeks at only its nearest neighbors, contrasting attention's global reach with the convolution's local view.
specs.caption: A convolution quietly polls its immediate neighbors; self-attention hands every patch a megaphone and lets the whole image join one loud, content-dependent conversation.

specs.anchorText: The whole stability of attention turns on that single factor of eight.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a friendly cartoon audio mixing console with a big rotary volume knob. On the left, the knob is cranked to maximum and one single loud speaker is blasting while all the other tiny speakers are silenced and shrinking away, looking overwhelmed, representing a saturated softmax where one patch swallows everything. On the right, the same knob is turned down to a balanced middle setting and a tidy row of small speakers all hum gently at similar comfortable volumes, representing a healthy, responsive softmax that still listens to every patch. A small cartoon scientist character happily adjusts the knob. Soft pastel blue, green, and warm orange palette, expressive simple shapes, minimal clutter, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear metaphor: dividing by the scale factor turns the volume back down so attention listens to everyone.
specs.alt: A cartoon audio mixer with a volume knob shown twice: cranked to maximum where one loud speaker drowns out all the silenced others, and turned to a balanced middle where a row of speakers all hum at similar gentle volumes, illustrating how the square-root scale factor keeps the softmax from saturating onto a single patch.
specs.caption: Without the scale factor one slightly-louder key drowns out the room; dividing by the square root of the head width turns the volume back to where attention still hears every patch.

specs.anchorText: a cat reassembled from patches in random order is no longer a cat.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a cartoon cat photograph that has been cut into square jigsaw-like patches. On the left, the patches are neatly in order and each patch wears a small numbered sticker, and together they form a clearly recognizable happy cartoon cat. On the right, the very same patches with their stickers removed are scrambled into a jumbled random arrangement, forming a confusing nonsense blob that no longer looks like a cat, with a small puzzled cartoon character scratching its head. A gentle arrow or simple visual flow connects the two. The metaphor: the little numbered position stickers are what let the model know where each patch belongs. Soft pastel orange, blue, and green palette, expressive simple shapes, minimal clutter, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear focused metaphor.
specs.alt: A cat photograph cut into square patches shown two ways: on the left the patches carry small position stickers and assemble into a recognizable cat, and on the right the same patches with stickers removed are scrambled into an unrecognizable blob while a puzzled character looks on, illustrating why positional embeddings are essential.
specs.caption: Self-attention treats patches as an unordered set, so without positional embeddings a cat reshuffled into random patches is just a bag of fur; the position stickers are the whole trick.

specs.anchorText: importing those biases through the teacher's predictions rather than rediscovering them from scratch.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a wise, friendly old cartoon owl-professor wearing small spectacles, representing a seasoned convolutional network teacher, sitting beside an eager young cartoon student robot, representing the data-efficient vision transformer. The wise owl gently whispers a hint into the young robot's ear, and a soft glowing thought-bubble passes a small helpful idea (drawn as a tidy little grid-pattern symbol suggesting locality knowledge) from teacher to student. The young robot has two small antennae or two badges on its chest, hinting at its two heads, one looking at a true-answer card and one looking toward the whispering teacher. Around them a modest stack of photos, far fewer than a giant pile, suggesting it learned from little data thanks to the mentor. Soft pastel green, warm orange, and blue palette, expressive simple shapes, minimal clutter, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, warm humor. One clear focused metaphor: the CNN mentor whispers its built-in biases to the ViT student.
specs.alt: A wise old owl-professor representing a convolutional network whispers a hint carrying a small grid-pattern idea into the ear of an eager young student robot representing a vision transformer, which has two badges for its class token and distillation token, illustrating how DeiT imports a CNN teacher's inductive bias through distillation instead of needing hundreds of millions of images.
specs.caption: DeiT lets the transformer skip the three-hundred-million-image apprenticeship by seating a wise convolutional mentor beside it to whisper the locality biases it never learned on its own.

specs.anchorText: whisper in small rooms, then shuffle the seating.
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a top-down cartoon view of a cozy banquet hall arranged as a neat grid of small square dinner tables bolted to the floor, each small table seating a few friendly cartoon guests who chat happily only with their own tablemates, representing local window attention in small rooms. A gentle curved arrow shows the next course: the tables stay exactly where they are, but half the guests cheerfully get up and swap to a neighboring table, so people who were at separate tables before now share a table and exchange news, representing the shifted-window step that lets information cross old boundaries. Keep the two table grids visibly offset to suggest the half-window shift. Soft pastel blue and warm orange palette, expressive simple shapes, minimal clutter, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear focused metaphor: tables stay put, guests swap seats.
specs.alt: A top-down banquet hall with a grid of fixed small dinner tables where guests chat only with their tablemates, and a curved arrow showing the next course where guests swap to neighboring tables so previously separated diners now share a table, illustrating Swin's window attention and shifted-window step that keeps attention local and cheap while letting information cross window boundaries.
specs.caption: Swin keeps attention cheap by whispering inside small fixed rooms, then shuffles the seating between courses so news from one window reaches the next without ever paying the quadratic bill.

specs.anchorText: comparing a transformer trained with a 2021 recipe to a CNN trained with a 2015 recipe
specs.prompt: Simple, cartoon-like educational illustration with clean lines and a warm color palette on a clean white background with generous margins. The scene: a friendly cartoon cooking contest framed as an unfair comparison. On the left, a cartoon convolution chef (an older-styled CNN character) is stuck with a tiny old camp stove and a meager basket of ingredients, producing a plain modest dish, representing an outdated 2015 training recipe. On the right, a cartoon transformer chef (a robot) cooks at a gleaming modern kitchen with a full pantry of fresh ingredients, producing a fancy dish, representing a modern 2021 recipe. A puzzled cartoon judge holds up a trophy toward the transformer, about to wrongly credit the win to the chef rather than to the kitchen. In a small calm inset, the same two chefs now share an identical modern kitchen and their two dishes look nearly the same size, hinting that with equal recipes the result is a tie. Soft pastel green, warm orange, and blue palette, expressive simple shapes, minimal clutter, XKCD-meets-Kurzgesagt style. Suitable for a technical textbook. No text or lettering in the image. Gentle, immediately understandable humor. One clear focused metaphor: the kitchen, not the chef, decided the contest.
specs.alt: A cooking-contest cartoon where a convolution chef cooks on an old camp stove with few ingredients while a transformer robot chef uses a modern kitchen and full pantry, and a judge is about to credit the transformer's win to the chef rather than the kitchen, with a small inset showing the two chefs tying when given the same modern kitchen, illustrating that recipe differences are often mistaken for architecture differences.
specs.caption: Crediting the transformer's win to attention is like crediting a fancier kitchen to the chef; hold the recipe fixed and the modern CNN and the ViT cook nearly the same dish.
